sources.entry: chrome-cdp-ex by Endeavor Yen - A zero-dependency Claude Code skill (68 commands) that connects to your *real* Chrome — logged-in tabs, cookies, live page state — to give the agent a perception layer: layout, visible styles, per-action "what changed" evidence, CSS-cascade-to-source tracing, and session replay/Playwright export. Notably rigorous about its own claims, with a dogfood benchmark gate t

summary.one_liner: A zero-dependency CLI and Claude Code skill that attaches to your already-running, logged-in Chrome over CDP so an agent can perceive, act on, and debug the live page.
summary.what_it_does: The tool attaches to an existing Chrome or Edge session through the DevTools Protocol, keeping the user's logins, cookies, and open tabs. `perceive` prints an accessibility tree with @ref handles and layout hints, and `perceive --since-action` shows only what the last action changed. `click`, `fill`, `press`, `drag`, `select`, and `scroll` send real CDP input events, and each action returns a one-line receipt naming the node addressed, the next command, and any dialog or download involved. `console` and `status` print source-mapped stack frames, `netlog --id N` shows one request's details, and `status --vitals` reports LCP, CLS, INP and long tasks. Screenshot commands (`shot`, `elshot`, `scanshot`, `responsive-audit`) capture pixels. The tool is usable as a Claude Code skill, a plain CLI, or a stdio MCP server. The README also describes redaction of secrets in output and opt-in guardrails such as allowed origins and denied actions.
use_cases: let an agent operate a tab where I am already logged in
inspect live page layout and visible styles for debugging
check what changed after a click or form fill
capture screenshots of a running web app or Electron window
read page content and network requests from a live session
run cron-style browser tasks against a persistent Chrome profile
notable: Attaches to the user's real logged-in Chrome session via the inspect toggle rather than launching a clean test browser
Action receipts report the addressed node, the element at the click point, dialogs answered, and downloads saved
Redacts tokens, auth headers, cookies, JWTs and secret-named field values in output by default
Exposes the same commands as a CLI, a Claude Code skill, and a stdio MCP server
Built on pasky/chrome-cdp-skill by Petr Baudis
caveats: Requires Node.js 22 or newer; doctor prints a Node 22 path if the system version is older
Hidden or minimized tabs may fail screenshots with Kind: hidden-tab, and other commands on hidden tabs can drop input
Redaction and guardrails are described as defense-in-depth for agents, not a security boundary
From Chrome 136, the --remote-debugging-port flag does not attach to the default profile; the inspect toggle is needed instead
